name: CISO scanner: stop flagging UUID / run-id shapes as secret.high-entropy-token
description:
## Finding (evidence)

`secret.high-entropy-token` is the single largest source of noise in the security gate, and it fires on identifiers, not credentials:

- `api/.codx/tasks/Agent: ciso/Done/shift-2026-11-18-14-35.62d592d3-7a93-4fcf-9fbd-a8ebc9dbfa2e.json` → **68 of its 69 findings** are `secret.high-entropy-token`, all on UUIDs and run ids: `doc_id`, `turn_id`, `cancellation_token_id` (see lines 45, 57, 127, 144, 146, 213 …).
- The previous shift recorded **1526 findings, all `secret.high-entropy-token` inside tracked `.codx/tasks/**` JSON**, and concluded in writing that *"the diff gate is permanently red for noise reasons"* (line 60 of that same file).
- Effective policy: `block_above=high`, `approval_above=medium`, `fail_closed=false` → a medium finding on a UUID requests approval, so a legitimate change is stopped by an identifier.

This is the highest-impact item because it trains everyone (and every agent) to ignore the gate: when a real credential arrives it will be finding 1527 of 1527.

## What to do

Make the entropy detector **shape-aware** — exclude known non-secret shapes before scoring entropy, instead of lowering the global threshold (lowering it would let real short tokens through):

1. Skip values that match canonical identifier shapes: UUID v4/v7, 32-hex, ULID, base32/base64 of a UUID, and the values of known identifier fields (`doc_id`, `turn_id`, `cancellation_token_id`, `chat_id`, `task_id`, `run_id`, `message_id`, `scan_id`, `session_id`, `correlation_id`).
2. Keep detecting real credentials unchanged: provider prefixes (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `sk-`, `xoxb-`, `AKIA…`, `AIza…`), private-key blocks, connection strings with credentials, JWTs.
3. Make the identifier-shape allowlist an explicit, documented scanner option (like the existing entropy/length thresholds) so a project can extend it without silencing the rule.
4. Do **not** close this by adding `ignore_rules: ["secret.high-entropy-token"]` — that removes the only credential detector from every gate.

Primary files: the secret detector table / entropy scorer and the scanner options surfaced in the Rules & policy tab, plus `docs/features/ciso.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `security_audit` on the shift transcript returns **0 `secret.high-entropy-token`** findings (from 68).
- [ ] A synthetic 40-char random token without a known prefix is **still** reported.
- [ ] `ghp_…`, `sk-…`, `AKIA…`, a PEM private key and a `post[REDACTED](26 chars) string are all **still** reported (regression tests).
- [ ] Every UUID field listed above is covered by a unit test that asserts no finding.
- [ ] The identifier-shape option is documented in `docs/features/ciso.md` under Rules & policy, and exposed next to the entropy threshold.
- [ ] Report the before/after finding count for the shift transcript in the task.
